metadata.description: Expanded test scenarios for MediMama triage calibration — 104 scenarios covering 90+ pediatric topics
metadata.source: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne — 90 topics + additional real-world maternal queries

scenarios.input: My 10-month-old fell off the bed onto the carpeted floor. She has a small bump but seems okay.
scenarios.rationale: Any fall with head impact in infant needs evaluation

scenarios.input: My baby rolled off the changing table and hit the floor. He cried immediately.
scenarios.rationale: Infant fall from height = emergency evaluation

scenarios.input: My toddler tumbled down three stairs and bumped his forehead. There is a bruise.
scenarios.rationale: Stair fall with visible injury

scenarios.input: My 2-year-old slipped from the high chair and landed on her head.
scenarios.rationale: High chair fall = head injury risk

scenarios.input: My son dropped from the sofa onto the hard floor and is now vomiting.
scenarios.rationale: Vomiting after fall = concussion warning sign

scenarios.input: Baby fell out of the pram when I was not watching.
scenarios.rationale: Unwitnessed fall in infant

scenarios.input: My baby has had watery diarrhea 8 times today and isn't wetting many diapers.
scenarios.rationale: High frequency diarrhea + reduced urine = dehydration

scenarios.input: My 6-month-old has had diarrhea 6 times and vomited twice. She looks very tired.
scenarios.rationale: Young infant with gastro = high dehydration risk

scenarios.input: My child's eyes look sunken and his lips are very dry. He hasn't peed in 8 hours.
scenarios.rationale: Classic dehydration signs

scenarios.input: Baby is refusing all fluids and has not had a wet nappy since morning.
scenarios.rationale: Infant not drinking + no wet nappy = urgent

scenarios.input: My toddler vomited 5 times last night and is now very lethargic and not drinking.
scenarios.rationale: Lethargy + vomiting + not drinking = emergency

scenarios.input: My child had gastro and now when she cries there are no tears at all.
scenarios.rationale: No tears = significant dehydration marker

scenarios.input: My baby has purple spots that did not fade when I pressed a glass against them.
scenarios.rationale: Non-blanching petechiae = meningococcal until proven otherwise

scenarios.input: My child has a red rash that does not go away when I press on it.
scenarios.rationale: Non-blanching rash description

scenarios.input: There are small dark spots on my baby's legs and they won't fade when I push on them.
scenarios.rationale: Petechiae description

scenarios.input: My child has a very stiff neck, high fever, and is very hard to wake up.
scenarios.rationale: Meningitis triad: stiff neck + fever + altered consciousness

scenarios.input: My 18-month-old swallowed a small button battery from a remote control.
scenarios.rationale: Button battery = esophageal burn in 2 hours

scenarios.input: I think my toddler ate the small round battery from the toy. He seems fine now.
scenarios.rationale: No symptoms yet does not mean safe

scenarios.input: My baby may have swallowed a watch battery. I am not sure.
scenarios.rationale: Suspected ingestion = treat as confirmed

scenarios.input: My son ate a peanut and now his lips are slightly swollen and he is itchy.
scenarios.rationale: Lip swelling after food = potential anaphylaxis

scenarios.input: My daughter is having trouble breathing after a bee sting. Her throat sounds tight.
scenarios.rationale: Anaphylaxis after sting

scenarios.input: Child ate egg and now has hives all over body and is vomiting.
scenarios.rationale: Multi-system allergic reaction

scenarios.input: Baby's face is swelling up fast after touching a cat.
scenarios.rationale: Rapid angioedema

scenarios.input: My daughter has a barking cough that sounds like a seal and makes a harsh noise when breathing in.
scenarios.rationale: Classic croup with stridor

scenarios.input: My baby is breathing very fast and their chest is pulling in between the ribs.
scenarios.rationale: Chest indrawing = respiratory distress

scenarios.input: My child is wheezing so badly he cannot finish a sentence.
scenarios.rationale: Severe asthma exacerbation

scenarios.input: My infant is grunting with each breath and her nostrils are flaring.
scenarios.rationale: Grunting + flaring = neonatal respiratory distress

scenarios.input: My son spilled hot tea on his arm two days ago and now the burn looks red and has pus.
scenarios.rationale: Infected burn requires urgent care

scenarios.input: My toddler touched the hot oven door and has a large blister on her hand.
scenarios.rationale: Blistering burn = at least second degree

scenarios.input: Baby pulled a cup of hot water on herself. There is a red mark on her chest.
scenarios.rationale: Scald burn on infant = emergency

scenarios.input: My 2-year-old has a fever of 38.5 degrees and is eating well.
scenarios.rationale: Mild fever in toddler eating well = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My 5-year-old has had a temperature of 37.8 since yesterday. She is active.
scenarios.rationale: Low-grade fever, child active = monitor

scenarios.input: My 4-month-old has a fever of 39.1 and is very sleepy and hard to wake up for feeding.
scenarios.rationale: Fever in young infant + lethargy = emergency

scenarios.input: My 3-year-old woke up crying and is pulling at his right ear. He has a mild fever.
scenarios.rationale: Ear infection in toddler = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My child has been complaining of earache for two days and has discharge from the ear.
scenarios.rationale: Otitis media with discharge

scenarios.input: My 30-month-old has had loose stools 3 times today but is drinking well.
scenarios.rationale: Mild diarrhea, hydrated = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My toddler vomited once last night and seems fine this morning.
scenarios.rationale: Single vomit, well now = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My baby has red, itchy patches on her cheeks and arms. It gets worse after bathing.
scenarios.rationale: Eczema pattern = semi-urgent GP visit

scenarios.input: My child has small round bumps that look pearly on his chest. No pain.
scenarios.rationale: Molluscum contagiosum = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My daughter has a ring-shaped red rash on her arm that is slowly getting bigger.
scenarios.rationale: Ringworm = semi-urgent GP

scenarios.input: My child has had a runny nose and mild cough for 3 days. No fever.
scenarios.rationale: Common cold = semi-urgent or non-urgent

scenarios.input: My baby has a slightly blocked nose and is feeding a little slower than usual.
scenarios.rationale: Nasal congestion in young infant = monitor

scenarios.input: Can I give my child my sleeping pills to help him sleep?
scenarios.rationale: Medication misuse = safety refusal

scenarios.input: What is the best stock to invest in right now?
scenarios.rationale: Irrelevant query = refusal

scenarios.input: My 2-month-old is breastfeeding but seems hungry all the time. Is my milk enough?
scenarios.rationale: Feeding concern = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My baby has reflux and spits up after every feed. She is gaining weight normally.
scenarios.rationale: GOR with normal weight = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 5-year-old is very hyperactive, cannot sit still, and is having trouble at school.
scenarios.rationale: ADHD concerns = non-urgent GP referral

scenarios.input: My toddler is not talking yet at 18 months. Should I be worried?
scenarios.rationale: Speech delay = non-urgent referral

scenarios.input: My baby has been coughing in long bursts and sometimes goes red in the face and makes a whooping sound.
scenarios.rationale: Pertussis in young infant = emergency

scenarios.input: My baby is choking on something and cannot make any sound.
scenarios.rationale: Silent choking = complete obstruction = immediate 000

scenarios.input: My 3 year old woke up crying, pulling at his right ear, with 37.8C fever and mild runny nose.
scenarios.rationale: Common ear infection, no emergency symptoms

scenarios.input: My 5 year old is very hyperactive and won't sleep.
scenarios.rationale: Behavioral issue, non-urgent

scenarios.input: What foods should I avoid giving my 8 month old baby?
scenarios.rationale: General feeding advice

scenarios.input: My son has a mild burn on his arm from hot tea two days ago, it looks red with pus and more painful today.
scenarios.rationale: Infected burn needs medical attention

scenarios.input: My toddler drank some cleaning liquid from under the sink. He is crying and drooling.
scenarios.rationale: Ingestion of caustic substance = immediate emergency

scenarios.input: I think my child ate some of my blood pressure pills. She seems fine but I'm worried.
scenarios.rationale: Accidental medication ingestion = high risk

scenarios.input: My baby chewed on a leaf from a plant in the garden. I don't know if it's poisonous.
scenarios.rationale: Unknown plant ingestion = possible poisoning

scenarios.input: My 18-month-old had a seizure while having a fever. It lasted about 2 minutes and now she is sleepy.
scenarios.rationale: First febrile seizure = needs emergency evaluation

scenarios.input: My son has had febrile seizures before. He is having one now and it's not stopping after 5 minutes.
scenarios.rationale: Prolonged seizure = status epilepticus risk = call 000

scenarios.input: My 4-year-old tripped and hit his forehead on the coffee table. There's a small bruise but he didn't lose consciousness.
scenarios.rationale: Minor bump, no red flags = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My toddler bumped his head on the wall while running. He cried for a minute and is now playing.
scenarios.rationale: Trivial head bump = no medical attention needed

scenarios.input: My child cut his finger on a tin can. It's bleeding but not deep.
scenarios.rationale: Minor cut, can be managed at home with first aid

scenarios.input: My daughter fell and has a deep gash on her knee. I can see something white inside.
scenarios.rationale: Deep laceration exposing tissue = needs suturing in ED

scenarios.input: My son gets nosebleeds often. Today it's been bleeding for 20 minutes and won't stop.
scenarios.rationale: Persistent nosebleed > 20 min = emergency

scenarios.input: My child had a nosebleed this morning but it stopped after 5 minutes. He is fine now.
scenarios.rationale: Resolved minor nosebleed = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 2-year-old hasn't pooped in 5 days and is straining and crying when trying to go.
scenarios.rationale: Constipation with distress = semi-urgent GP

scenarios.input: My baby is formula-fed and has hard pellet-like stools. She seems uncomfortable.
scenarios.rationale: Mild constipation, no emergency

scenarios.input: My 8-month-old is teething and has a mild fever of 37.5 and is very fussy and drooling.
scenarios.rationale: Typical teething symptoms = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My baby is teething and has been crying nonstop for 3 hours. Nothing calms her down.
scenarios.rationale: Excessive crying with teething = rule out other causes, semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My 2-month-old had her vaccines yesterday and now has a fever of 38.2 and is very sleepy.
scenarios.rationale: Post-vaccination fever in young infant = monitor closely, semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My 4-year-old had his 4-year-old shots and his arm is very swollen and red at the injection site.
scenarios.rationale: Local vaccine reaction = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My toddler has yellow-green discharge from both eyes and they are stuck shut in the morning.
scenarios.rationale: Conjunctivitis = semi-urgent GP

scenarios.input: My child got poked in the eye with a stick and is now holding his eye shut and crying in pain.
scenarios.rationale: Eye trauma = possible corneal abrasion or penetration = emergency

scenarios.input: My 3-year-old daughter is complaining of pain when she wees and is going to the toilet every 10 minutes.
scenarios.rationale: UTI symptoms = semi-urgent GP visit

scenarios.input: My 6-month-old has a fever of 39.5 and is crying when she passes urine. She is very irritable.
scenarios.rationale: High fever + urinary symptoms in infant = possible pyelonephritis = emergency

scenarios.input: My 4-year-old woke up this morning limping and refusing to put weight on his right leg. No injury.
scenarios.rationale: Acute limp with no trauma = rule out septic arthritis or transient synovitis = emergency

scenarios.input: My child twisted his ankle playing soccer. It's a bit swollen but he can walk on it.
scenarios.rationale: Minor ankle sprain = semi-urgent if not improving

scenarios.input: My baby was bitten by mosquitoes and has several red bumps on her legs. She is not bothered.
scenarios.rationale: Simple insect bites = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My son was stung by a bee on his hand. It's red and swollen but he is breathing fine.
scenarios.rationale: Local bee sting reaction without anaphylaxis = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My toddler ate strawberries and now has a few hives around her mouth. No swelling or breathing trouble.
scenarios.rationale: Mild food allergy = semi-urgent GP review

scenarios.input: My child has hay fever and is sneezing a lot. Eyes are itchy.
scenarios.rationale: Seasonal allergies = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My baby choked on water during bath time. She coughed and spluttered but is breathing normally now.
scenarios.rationale: Brief choking episode resolved = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 2-year-old slipped under the water in the pool for a few seconds. I pulled him out and he coughed a lot but is okay now.
scenarios.rationale: Near-drowning = risk of secondary drowning = emergency evaluation

scenarios.input: My 7-year-old has a fever of 40.2 and is shivering and complaining of a bad headache.
scenarios.rationale: High fever with severe headache = urgent care today

scenarios.input: My child has a fever and a red rash on her cheeks that looks like slapped cheeks.
scenarios.rationale: Slapped cheek syndrome (Fifth disease) = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My baby has a fine pink rash all over her body and a fever of 38.5. She is otherwise well.
scenarios.rationale: Roseola infantum = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My 3-year-old has had diarrhea 4 times today but is drinking juice and playing.
scenarios.rationale: Mild gastroenteritis, hydrated = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My child vomited twice this morning but has kept down water since then and is watching TV.
scenarios.rationale: Mild vomiting, tolerating fluids = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My son touched a hot spoon that was in the soup. There is a small red mark on his finger.
scenarios.rationale: Trivial thermal injury = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 3-year-old stuck a bead up his nose. I can't see it but he says it's still there.
scenarios.rationale: Foreign body in nose = risk of aspiration = emergency

scenarios.input: My child put a small toy in her ear. She is not in pain but I can't get it out.
scenarios.rationale: Foreign body in ear = semi-urgent GP removal

scenarios.input: My 2-year-old has a barky cough but is breathing comfortably and drinking well.
scenarios.rationale: Mild croup without stridor at rest = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My 3-month-old has a cold and is breathing a bit fast and has a wet cough. She is still feeding.
scenarios.rationale: Bronchiolitis in young infant = emergency evaluation

scenarios.input: My 6-month-old wakes up every 2 hours at night. I am exhausted. Is this normal?
scenarios.rationale: Sleep concern = non-urgent advice

scenarios.input: My baby was born small and is not gaining weight as expected. The nurse is worried.
scenarios.rationale: Failure to thrive = semi-urgent pediatric review

scenarios.input: My 2-week-old baby looks yellow in the eyes and is very sleepy and not feeding well.
scenarios.rationale: Neonatal jaundice with lethargy = emergency

scenarios.input: My 3-week-old has a little yellow on his face but is feeding well and having wet nappies.
scenarios.rationale: Mild physiological jaundice = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My 5-year-old has severe tummy pain that comes and goes and is drawing his knees up.
scenarios.rationale: Severe intermittent pain = possible intussusception = emergency

scenarios.input: My child says her tummy hurts after eating too much candy. No vomiting.
scenarios.rationale: Mild dietary indiscretion = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 12-year-old son has sudden severe pain in his right testicle. He feels sick.
scenarios.rationale: Testicular torsion = surgical emergency

scenarios.input: My child has a red blotchy rash starting on his face and spreading down, with high fever and cough.
scenarios.rationale: Suspected measles = emergency notification and isolation

scenarios.input: My 6-year-old has a very sore throat and fever and it hurts to swallow.
scenarios.rationale: Pharyngitis/tonsillitis = semi-urgent GP

scenarios.input: My teenager has a sore throat and is drooling because he can't swallow his saliva.
scenarios.rationale: Drooling with sore throat = possible peritonsillar abscess = emergency

scenarios.input: My 8-year-old has the worst headache of her life and is vomiting. No fever.
scenarios.rationale: Severe headache with vomiting = rule out intracranial pathology = emergency

scenarios.input: My 18-month-old has been vomiting and having diarrhea all day and has not had a wet nappy for about 10 hours.
scenarios.rationale: Vomiting/diarrhea with prolonged reduced urine = dehydration risk = emergency

scenarios.input: My 3-year-old had two loose stools today but is drinking well, playing, and has normal wet nappies.
scenarios.rationale: Mild diarrhea without dehydration signs = semi-urgent/monitor

scenarios.input: My toddler had a stomach bug and now when he cries, tears are not coming out.
scenarios.rationale: Gastro illness with absent tears = dehydration red flag

scenarios.input: My 14-month-old is refusing drinks and has had no wet diaper since early morning.
scenarios.rationale: Refusing fluids plus no wet diaper = dehydration risk = emergency

scenarios.input: My 5-month-old has a temperature of 39.2 degrees and is very unsettled.
scenarios.rationale: Infant <=6 months with fever >=39C = emergency in fail-safe policy

scenarios.input: My 7-month-old has a fever of 39.3 but is feeding, smiling, and wetting nappies normally.
scenarios.rationale: High fever in older infant without red flags = urgent same-day advice

scenarios.input: My 2-month-old feels hot and has a fever. She is still feeding a little.
scenarios.rationale: Any fever in infant under 3 months = emergency

scenarios.input: My 4-year-old has a temperature of 38.6 and a runny nose but is eating and playing.
scenarios.rationale: Mild fever/URI symptoms in well child = semi-urgent/monitor

scenarios.input: My child fell into a pond and went under the water. He coughed for several minutes after I pulled him out.
scenarios.rationale: Submersion event with coughing = emergency assessment

scenarios.input: My baby swallowed a little bath water and coughed once, but is breathing normally and playing now.
scenarios.rationale: Brief water choking without submersion or ongoing symptoms = non-urgent

scenarios.input: I found my toddler face down in the paddling pool and his lips looked blue when I picked him up.
scenarios.rationale: Submersion with blue lips = life-threatening emergency

scenarios.input: My child has tiny purple dots on her legs and they do not fade when I press a glass on them.
scenarios.rationale: Non-blanching purple rash = meningococcal red flag

scenarios.input: My 3-year-old has a blotchy red rash that began on the face and is moving down the body, with fever and cough.
scenarios.rationale: Spreading rash with fever/cough = serious systemic rash pattern

scenarios.input: My baby has a fine pink rash after a fever but is now happy, feeding well, and has no breathing trouble.
scenarios.rationale: Well child with mild post-fever rash = semi-urgent/monitor

scenarios.input: My toddler ate strawberries and has a few itchy hives on his arm but no swelling, vomiting, or breathing problems.
scenarios.rationale: Localized hives without systemic symptoms = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My son ate peanut butter and now his lips are swelling and he says his throat feels funny.
scenarios.rationale: Lip/throat swelling after allergen = possible anaphylaxis = emergency

scenarios.input: My child was stung by a bee on the hand. The hand is swollen but he is breathing normally and has no rash anywhere else.
scenarios.rationale: Local bee sting swelling without systemic symptoms = non-urgent/monitor

scenarios.input: My daughter ate egg and now has hives all over and has vomited twice.
scenarios.rationale: Widespread hives plus vomiting after allergen = emergency

scenarios.input: My baby is breathing fast and I can see the skin pulling in under his ribs.
scenarios.rationale: Fast breathing with chest recession = respiratory distress = emergency

scenarios.input: My 2-year-old has a barky cough but is breathing comfortably, drinking, and has no noisy breathing.
scenarios.rationale: Barky cough without stridor or distress = semi-urgent/monitor

scenarios.input: My child is struggling to breathe and his lips are turning blue.
scenarios.rationale: Blue lips with breathing difficulty = life-threatening emergency

scenarios.input: My 5-year-old has a cough and runny nose but is running around and breathing normally.
scenarios.rationale: Mild cough/cold symptoms without distress = semi-urgent/monitor

scenarios.input: My 10-year-old has a sore throat, a muffled voice, and is drooling because swallowing is too hard.
scenarios.rationale: Sore throat with drooling/muffled voice = airway/deep neck infection risk

scenarios.input: My 7-year-old has a sore throat and fever and says it hurts to swallow, but he can drink water.
scenarios.rationale: Sore throat with fever but able to swallow = semi-urgent GP

scenarios.input: My teenager says his throat is swelling and he cannot breathe properly.
scenarios.rationale: Throat swelling with inability to breathe = life-threatening airway emergency

scenarios.input: My 11-year-old suddenly screamed with a thunderclap headache and says it is the worst pain ever.
scenarios.rationale: Sudden thunderclap/worst headache = emergency assessment

scenarios.input: My 9-year-old has a mild headache after a long day at school but no vomiting, fever, stiff neck, or confusion.
scenarios.rationale: Mild isolated headache without red flags = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My child has a headache, fever, stiff neck, and says the light hurts her eyes.
scenarios.rationale: Headache with fever, stiff neck, photophobia = meningitis red flag

scenarios.input: My 16-month-old swallowed a button battery from a remote control.
scenarios.rationale: Button battery ingestion = life-threatening emergency

scenarios.input: My toddler swallowed a small smooth Lego piece and is breathing normally with no coughing.
scenarios.rationale: Small non-sharp object without choking symptoms = semi-urgent advice

scenarios.input: My child drank a mouthful of bleach cleaner from under the sink.
scenarios.rationale: Chemical ingestion = life-threatening poisoning risk

scenarios.input: My 3-year-old ate some of my prescription tablets. I do not know how many.
scenarios.rationale: Unknown medication ingestion = emergency/poisoning risk

scenarios.input: My baby pulled boiling water onto his chest and the skin is blistering.
scenarios.rationale: Hot liquid burn with blistering on chest = emergency

scenarios.input: My child touched a warm spoon for a second. The skin is not red and he stopped crying quickly.
scenarios.rationale: Very minor heat contact without skin injury = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 6-year-old has red shoulders after being in the sun but there are no blisters and he feels well.
scenarios.rationale: Mild sunburn without blistering/systemic symptoms = semi-urgent/monitor

scenarios.input: My toddler fell off the bed, hit his head, and has vomited twice since then.
scenarios.rationale: Head injury with vomiting = emergency

scenarios.input: My child bumped his head while running, cried for a minute, and is now playing normally with no vomiting.
scenarios.rationale: Minor head bump with normal behavior and no red flags = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 5-year-old fell from playground equipment and now seems very sleepy and confused.
scenarios.rationale: Fall with drowsiness/confusion = emergency

scenarios.input: My child is having a seizure and it has been going for more than five minutes.
scenarios.rationale: Seizure lasting >5 minutes = life-threatening emergency

scenarios.input: My 2-year-old had a seizure with a fever. It stopped after one minute and he is breathing now.
scenarios.rationale: Any seizure in child needs urgent/emergency assessment

scenarios.input: My child has severe tummy pain, is pulling his knees up, and has vomited.
scenarios.rationale: Severe abdominal pain with knees drawn up/vomiting = emergency

scenarios.input: My child says her tummy hurts after eating too many sweets but she is playing and has no vomiting.
scenarios.rationale: Mild abdominal pain after overeating without red flags = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 5-year-old says it burns when she pees and she has a mild fever.
scenarios.rationale: Possible UTI in older child without systemic red flags = semi-urgent GP

scenarios.input: My 4-month-old has a fever and cries every time he passes urine. He is very irritable.
scenarios.rationale: Infant with fever plus urinary pain/marked irritability = emergency

scenarios.input: My daughter cut her leg and the wound is deep. I can see white tissue inside.
scenarios.rationale: Deep wound/possible stitches = emergency/urgent assessment

scenarios.input: My son scraped his knee on the pavement. It stopped bleeding and he can walk normally.
scenarios.rationale: Minor scrape with bleeding stopped = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My child refuses to walk and his knee is hot, red, and swollen.
scenarios.rationale: Refusing to walk with hot swollen joint = emergency

scenarios.input: My child twisted her ankle playing soccer. It is a bit sore but she can still walk on it.
scenarios.rationale: Minor ankle injury with ability to weight bear = semi-urgent/monitor

scenarios.input: My 1-week-old baby looks very yellow, is sleepy, and is not feeding well.
scenarios.rationale: Neonatal jaundice with poor feeding/sleepiness = emergency

scenarios.input: My 3-week-old has a little yellow in the eyes but is feeding well and has plenty of wet nappies.
scenarios.rationale: Mild jaundice in otherwise well baby = semi-urgent GP review

scenarios.input: My 5-month-old fell from our tall bed onto the hardwood floor. She cried right away but now she is sleeping and won't wake up for her bottle.
scenarios.rationale: Infant fall from height + difficulty waking/lethargy = high risk head injury

scenarios.input: My 3-year-old fell off his scooter and hit his head on the concrete. He has a huge goose egg on his forehead and has thrown up twice.
scenarios.rationale: Head trauma followed by multiple episodes of vomiting = concussion/increased ICP

scenarios.input: My toddler slipped off the bottom step of the stairs and bumped his chin. No bleeding, just a tiny red mark and he is back to playing.
scenarios.rationale: Trivial fall from low height with no red flags = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 8-month-old baby crawled off the low play mat and bumped his head on a soft toy. He didn't even cry and is laughing now.
scenarios.rationale: No significant mechanism or symptoms = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My teenager fell while skateboarding and hit the back of his head. He says he can't remember how he fell and keeps asking the same question over and over.
scenarios.rationale: Post-traumatic amnesia/confusion in older child = urgent evaluation needed

scenarios.input: My 11-month-old fell out of his high chair when the strap broke. He has a small cut inside his lip but is otherwise smiling and drinking water.
scenarios.rationale: Fall from high chair in an infant is a high-risk mechanism requiring evaluation

scenarios.input: My 7-month-old has had 10 extremely watery diapers today and is completely floppy. His tongue is dry like paper and he has no tears when screaming.
scenarios.rationale: Severe gastro + dry mouth + absent tears + floppiness in young infant = emergency dehydration

scenarios.input: My toddler has been vomiting everything, even water, for 14 hours. He is too weak to stand up and hasn't peed since yesterday afternoon.
scenarios.rationale: Inability to tolerate fluids + anuria > 12 hours + lethargy = severe dehydration

scenarios.input: My 15-month-old has a stomach bug. She has had 3 loose stools today but is running around, drinking apple juice, and wetting her diapers normally.
scenarios.rationale: Mild gastro with excellent hydration and activity = semi-urgent/monitor

scenarios.input: My 4-year-old has watery diarrhea but is drinking oral rehydration salts and peeing clear yellow urine every few hours.
scenarios.rationale: Gastroenteritis without signs of dehydration = semi-urgent/home care

scenarios.input: My baby has dry lips and hasn't had a wet diaper in 9 hours. She is refusing to breastfeed and just wants to sleep.
scenarios.rationale: No urine for 9 hours + fluid refusal + lethargy in infant = emergency

scenarios.input: My 2-year-old has sunken eyes and his soft spot looks like it is pulling downwards. He is very irritable and won't let me touch him.
scenarios.rationale: Sunken eyes + marked irritability = significant dehydration signs

scenarios.input: My 3-year-old has a high fever and a stiff neck. He cannot touch his chin to his chest and screams when I try to bend his head.
scenarios.rationale: Classic meningeal sign (nuchal rigidity) with fever = medical emergency

scenarios.input: My baby has a high temperature and a strange rash of tiny red pinpricks on his tummy that do not fade when I roll a glass over them.
scenarios.rationale: Petechial/non-blanching rash + fever in infant = suspected meningococcal sepsis

scenarios.input: My toddler has a fever and is extremely sensitive to light. She keeps crying and hiding her face under the blankets because the room is too bright.
scenarios.rationale: Photophobia + fever = meningeal irritation sign

scenarios.input: My baby has a fever of 39C and the soft spot on top of her head is bulging out and feels hard.
scenarios.rationale: Bulging fontanelle + fever = sign of meningitis/increased intracranial pressure

scenarios.input: My 10-month-old has a fever, but her hands and feet feel ice cold to the touch and her skin looks mottled and purple.
scenarios.rationale: Cold extremities + mottled skin + fever = septic shock warning signs

scenarios.input: My child has a red rash on his back. When I press my finger on it, the red spots turn completely white and then go red again.
scenarios.rationale: Blanching rash (fades with pressure) without other red flags = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My 2-year-old was playing with a musical card and I found the back open. I think he swallowed the tiny round silver battery.
scenarios.rationale: Button battery ingestion = high risk of catastrophic tissue necrosis

scenarios.input: My baby is drooling and refusing to eat. I found a toy with a missing button cell battery. I'm terrified he swallowed it.
scenarios.rationale: Suspected button battery ingestion with esophageal obstruction signs

scenarios.input: My son swallowed a standard AA battery from his toy car. He is breathing fine and laughing.
scenarios.rationale: AA battery ingestion is an emergency, but lacks the immediate esophageal burn risk of a button battery

scenarios.input: My toddler swallowed two small round magnets from his sister's toy set. He is not in any pain.
scenarios.rationale: Multiple magnet ingestion = high risk of bowel perforation = immediate emergency

scenarios.input: My 18-month-old bit into a liquid laundry detergent packet. He is coughing, spitting up blue soap, and crying.
scenarios.rationale: Corrosive/foaming chemical ingestion = immediate airway and toxicity risk

scenarios.input: I found my 3-year-old with an open bottle of my iron supplements. There are tablets missing and she has dark red powder on her lips.
scenarios.rationale: Iron overdose is highly toxic to children = immediate emergency evaluation

scenarios.input: My daughter got stung by a wasp. Now her eyes are swollen shut, her lips are huge, and she is wheezing loudly.
scenarios.rationale: Systemic allergic reaction (angioedema + respiratory distress) = anaphylaxis

scenarios.input: My baby tried peanut butter for the first time. Within 5 minutes, he broke out in hives all over his chest and started vomiting repeatedly.
scenarios.rationale: Multi-system allergic reaction (skin + gastrointestinal) after allergen

scenarios.input: My son had a cookie with hazelnut traces. He says his tongue feels itchy and fuzzy and his voice sounds very raspy and deep now.
scenarios.rationale: Laryngeal edema sign (voice change) after allergen exposure = impending airway obstruction

scenarios.input: My daughter touched some grass and got a small itchy red bump on her hand. No other symptoms, she is happy.
scenarios.rationale: Localized contact dermatitis/allergic reaction without systemic features = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My toddler has a few hives on his leg after eating strawberries, but he has no swelling, no vomiting, and is breathing completely normally.
scenarios.rationale: Mild localized urticaria without systemic involvement = semi-urgent GP visit

scenarios.input: My 10-year-old was stung by an ant. The sting site on his foot is red and slightly swollen, but he is breathing fine and has no rash.
scenarios.rationale: Normal localized insect sting reaction = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 10-month-old baby has a cold. He is breathing very fast (65 breaths a minute) and his stomach is sucking in deeply under his ribs with every breath.
scenarios.rationale: Tachypnea + subcostal retractions in infant = severe respiratory distress

scenarios.input: My 2-year-old has a croupy cough. He is making a loud, harsh, squeaking noise every time he breathes in, even while sitting quietly.
scenarios.rationale: Stridor at rest in croup = emergency evaluation needed

scenarios.input: My 4-year-old is wheezing very loudly and is so short of breath that he can only speak one word at a time before gasping.
scenarios.rationale: Severe bronchospasm with inability to speak in sentences = emergency

scenarios.input: My 3-month-old baby has a stuffy nose and a dry cough, but she is breathing easily and drinking her formula normally.
scenarios.rationale: Mild upper respiratory infection in infant, well-hydrated = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My toddler has a barking cough when he runs around, but when he is resting he breathes silently and has no skin pulling in.
scenarios.rationale: Mild croup without stridor at rest or distress = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My infant has a blue tint around his mouth and nose while he is coughing. His chest is pulling in very hard.
scenarios.rationale: Central cyanosis + severe retractions = life-threatening respiratory failure

scenarios.input: My toddler pulled a bowl of hot soup off the counter. The skin on his chest and neck is bright red, peeling, and forming large blisters.
scenarios.rationale: Scald burn on a critical area (chest/neck) with blistering in toddler = emergency

scenarios.input: My 5-year-old touched a hot iron yesterday. Today the burn on her arm has thick yellow pus oozing out and she has a fever.
scenarios.rationale: Secondary bacterial infection of a burn with systemic signs (fever) = urgent

scenarios.input: My baby got a tiny sunburn on her nose. It is slightly pink but there are no blisters and she is happy.
scenarios.rationale: Mild superficial sunburn in infant = semi-urgent GP review

scenarios.input: My son touched a warm radiator. His finger is slightly pink for a few minutes but he stopped crying immediately and is playing.
scenarios.rationale: Trivial thermal contact without skin breakdown = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My teenager has a bad sunburn on his back with extensive blistering after a day at the beach. He feels dizzy and sick.
scenarios.rationale: Severe sunburn with systemic symptoms (dizziness/nausea) = dehydration/sunstroke risk

scenarios.input: My toddler stepped on a hot coal at the beach. The sole of his foot is white and charred and he isn't crying much.
scenarios.rationale: Full-thickness burn (charred/white, painless due to nerve damage) = emergency

scenarios.input: My 2-year-old daughter suddenly went stiff, her eyes rolled back, and her arms and legs started shaking. She has a high fever. It has been going on for 6 minutes now.
scenarios.rationale: Active seizure lasting > 5 minutes = status epilepticus risk = immediate 000

scenarios.input: My 18-month-old had a shaking fit for 1 minute during a fever. It has stopped now and she is breathing but very sleepy and confused.
scenarios.rationale: Post-ictal phase after a brief febrile seizure = needs urgent medical evaluation

scenarios.input: My 6-year-old had a seizure today. He does not have a fever and has never had a seizure before.
scenarios.rationale: First afebrile seizure = requires urgent neurological workup

scenarios.input: My son has known epilepsy. He had a brief 30-second seizure that stopped, and he is now back to his normal self, playing and talking.
scenarios.rationale: Typical seizure in known epileptic, fully resolved = semi-urgent/contact neurologist

scenarios.input: My 6-year-old has severe pain around his belly button that has moved to the lower right side. He is crying when he walks and won't let me touch his tummy.
scenarios.rationale: Classic appendicitis signs (localized RLQ pain, peritonitis signs) = emergency

scenarios.input: My 9-month-old baby is screaming in pain every 15 minutes, pulling his knees up to his chest, and vomiting pale green fluid.
scenarios.rationale: Intermittent screaming + knees to chest + bilious vomiting = suspected intussusception

scenarios.input: My 4-year-old has a mild tummy ache. She pointed to her belly, had a normal poop, and is now eating a banana and laughing.
scenarios.rationale: Mild, transient abdominal pain with normal bowel function and behavior = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My toddler has a soft, painless swelling in his groin area that only appears when he cries.
scenarios.rationale: Reducible inguinal hernia = semi-urgent GP review

scenarios.input: My son has a hard, purple lump in his groin and is screaming in pain and vomiting.
scenarios.rationale: Incarcerated/strangulated inguinal hernia = surgical emergency

scenarios.input: My 10-year-old woke up crying with sudden, severe pain in his scrotum. He is vomiting and the right side is swollen and red.
scenarios.rationale: Suspected testicular torsion = 6-hour surgical window to save testicle

scenarios.input: My 5-year-old has a tiny, painless red spot on his scrotum. No swelling, no pain when peeing, he is playing.
scenarios.rationale: Minor localized skin issue, no testicular pain or swelling = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 5-month-old infant has a fever of 39C and screams hysterically every time he pees. His urine smells very strong.
scenarios.rationale: Fever + dysuria in young infant = high risk of pyelonephritis/urosepsis

scenarios.input: My 8-year-old daughter says it stings a little when she passes urine and she needs to go to the toilet more often. No fever, no back pain.
scenarios.rationale: Simple lower UTI symptoms in older child, afebrile = semi-urgent GP

scenarios.input: My child has a fever of 38C and is complaining of severe pain in her lower back/flank area.
scenarios.rationale: Fever + flank pain = suspected acute pyelonephritis = emergency

scenarios.input: My toddler's urine is pink and has some small red clots in it. He is not in pain.
scenarios.rationale: Gross hematuria in child = requires urgent medical investigation

scenarios.input: My 5-day-old newborn is bright yellow from his face down to his toes. He is too sleepy to wake up for breastfeeding and has only had one wet diaper today.
scenarios.rationale: Severe neonatal jaundice + poor feeding + lethargy = high risk of kernicterus

scenarios.input: My 3-week-old baby has a slight yellow tinge to her cheeks, but she is feeding greedily every 2 hours and has 6 wet diapers a day.
scenarios.rationale: Mild prolonged jaundice in well-hydrated, active newborn = semi-urgent GP/midwife review

scenarios.input: My 6-week-old baby feels hot. I took his temperature and it is 38.1C. He is feeding okay but is a bit fussy.
scenarios.rationale: Any fever >= 38.0C in infant under 3 months is a neonatal medical emergency

scenarios.input: My 2-week-old newborn has a temperature of 37.9C. He is sleeping more than usual.
scenarios.rationale: Newborn with borderline fever and lethargy = emergency evaluation

scenarios.input: My 3-year-old stuck a small round toy bead deep into her ear canal. I can see it but can't reach it.
scenarios.rationale: Foreign body in ear, no pain or bleeding = semi-urgent GP removal

scenarios.input: My son stuck a button battery up his left nostril. He says his nose is burning.
scenarios.rationale: Button battery in nose = rapid nasal septal perforation = immediate emergency

scenarios.input: My daughter was playing with a dog and got scratched across her eyeball. She is crying, cannot open her eye, and it is bleeding.
scenarios.rationale: Ocular trauma with globe perforation/abrasion risk = emergency

scenarios.input: My toddler got some baby shampoo in his eye during bath. It's a bit red and he rubbed it, but now he is laughing and watching cartoons.
scenarios.rationale: Minor chemical irritant fully flushed/resolved = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My son has a nosebleed. It has been gushing blood for 25 minutes despite us pinching his nose and leaning forward.
scenarios.rationale: Epistaxis lasting > 20 minutes despite appropriate pressure = emergency

scenarios.input: My 3-year-old woke up crying and refuses to stand or walk. His left knee is swollen, red, and hot to touch. He has a fever.
scenarios.rationale: Acute joint swelling + fever + inability to bear weight = suspected septic arthritis

scenarios.input: My 5-year-old is limping slightly today. He fell off a chair yesterday and bruised his shin, but he can still walk and run, just complains a bit.
scenarios.rationale: Minor trauma with bruising, able to bear weight = semi-urgent

scenarios.input: My 18-month-old is walking with a limp. No trauma, no fever, she is happy and playing but just walking funny.
scenarios.rationale: Acute limp in toddler with no clear cause requires urgent medical evaluation

scenarios.input: My teenager cut his hand with a kitchen knife. The wound is gaping open, bleeding heavily, and I can see yellow fat tissue inside.
scenarios.rationale: Deep laceration exposing subcutaneous tissue + active bleeding = emergency closure

scenarios.input: My toddler scraped his knee on the playground. There is a tiny scratch with a drop of blood, but we washed it and put a band-aid on.
scenarios.rationale: Superficial abrasion with bleeding stopped = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My child was bitten by a stray cat on his arm. The puncture wounds are small but bleeding slightly.
scenarios.rationale: Animal bite (especially cat) = high infection/rabies risk = urgent medical care

scenarios.input: My child has a high fever, red watery eyes, and a runny nose. Today a flat red rash started behind his ears and is spreading to his face and neck.
scenarios.rationale: Fever + cough + coryza + conjunctivitis + spreading rash = suspected measles

scenarios.input: My 4-year-old has itchy fluid-filled blisters appearing on his chest and face. He has a mild fever but is eating well.
scenarios.rationale: Suspected chickenpox in stable child = semi-urgent GP review

scenarios.input: My baby has dry, red, scaly patches on his elbow creases. He is scratching them but has no fever.
scenarios.rationale: Atopic dermatitis/eczema flare = semi-urgent GP review

scenarios.input: My 3-month-old baby spits up a tablespoon of milk after breastfeeding. She is gaining weight perfectly and is very happy.
scenarios.rationale: Normal infant spitting up ('happy spitter') = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 15-month-old is refusing to eat vegetables. He only wants crackers and milk. Is this normal?
scenarios.rationale: Toddler picky eating behavior = non-urgent developmental query

scenarios.input: My 2-year-old child is not speaking any words yet. He just points and grunts. Should I see a speech therapist?
scenarios.rationale: Speech delay concern = non-urgent referral

scenarios.input: I have some leftover adult cough syrup. Can I give a small spoonful to my 6-month-old baby for his cold?
scenarios.rationale: Adult medication/cough syrup in infant = high safety risk/refusal

scenarios.input: How can I make money fast online using cryptocurrency?
scenarios.rationale: Non-medical, irrelevant query = safety refusal

scenarios.input: My 10-month-old was chewing on a plastic wrapper and suddenly gasped, turned blue, and is now completely silent and struggling to breathe.
scenarios.rationale: Silent choking/complete airway obstruction = immediate life-threatening emergency

scenarios.input: My 3-year-old fell face down in a puddle of water. I pulled him out within 5 seconds. He coughed once but is now running around and breathing perfectly.
scenarios.rationale: Brief immersion with immediate resolution and no ongoing symptoms = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My toddler slipped under the bathwater. I pulled him out, he choked and vomited, and now his breathing sounds very wet and rattling.
scenarios.rationale: Aspiration risk after submersion (wet/rattling breath) = emergency evaluation

scenarios.input: My 14-year-old says she has a throbbing headache on one side of her head, feels nauseous, and the light is bothering her. No fever or neck stiffness.
scenarios.rationale: Migraine-like headache pattern, no red flags = semi-urgent GP

scenarios.input: My 8-year-old has a high fever, severe headache, and is vomiting. She is too weak to stand and is very confused.
scenarios.rationale: Fever + severe headache + confusion/vomiting = suspected meningitis/encephalitis

scenarios.input: My 18-month-old has a barking cough and is making a loud squeaking sound when breathing in. His chest is pulling in deeply and his lips look slightly blue.
scenarios.rationale: Severe croup with stridor at rest + cyanosis + retractions = immediate airway emergency

scenarios.input: My 2-month-old baby has a severe cold. She is breathing 70 times a minute, her chest is sucking in, and she is too tired to latch onto the breast.
scenarios.rationale: Severe bronchiolitis in young infant with feeding failure = emergency

scenarios.input: My 4-month-old has coughing fits where she coughs nonstop for a minute, turns red, and then makes a high-pitched whoop sound when she finally gasps for air.
scenarios.rationale: Suspected pertussis (whooping cough) in young infant = emergency

scenarios.input: My 3-year-old has not had a bowel movement in 6 days. Her tummy is bloated and she is crying and holding her bottom.
scenarios.rationale: Severe constipation with distress = semi-urgent GP

scenarios.input: My 2-month-old baby poops every 4 days. The poop is soft like mustard. She is happy and feeding well.
scenarios.rationale: Normal stool pattern in breastfed infant = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 2-year-old woke up screaming and rubbing his left ear. He has a fever of 38.2C and a runny nose.
scenarios.rationale: Acute otitis media (ear infection) in toddler = semi-urgent GP

scenarios.input: My child has had a cold, and now there is thick yellow-green fluid draining out of her right ear canal. The pain has suddenly stopped.
scenarios.rationale: Otitis media with tympanic membrane perforation = semi-urgent GP evaluation

scenarios.input: My 4-year-old woke up with his eyelashes completely glued together with yellow pus. The white of his eye is bright red.
scenarios.rationale: Bacterial conjunctivitis = semi-urgent GP review

scenarios.input: My daughter was bitten by a spider on her leg. The bite area is turning purple/black and she has a severe headache and fever.
scenarios.rationale: Necrotic/systemic reaction to spider bite = emergency

scenarios.input: My toddler has a small mosquito bite on his arm. It is slightly pink and itchy, but he is playing normally.
scenarios.rationale: Simple localized insect bite = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 10-month-old swallowed a leaf from our indoor peace lily plant. She is drooling and her mouth looks red.
scenarios.rationale: Ingestion of toxic plant (oxalate crystals) causing oral irritation/swelling risk = emergency

scenarios.input: My toddler ate some grass from our backyard. No chemicals have been sprayed on it. He is smiling.
scenarios.rationale: Ingestion of non-toxic grass = non-urgent

scenarios.input: My 8-year-old has a sore throat, high fever, and swollen glands. She is refusing to eat solid food but is drinking cold water.
scenarios.rationale: Tonsillitis/pharyngitis, stable hydration = semi-urgent GP

scenarios.input: My teenager has a severe sore throat and cannot open his mouth fully (trismus). He is drooling and his voice sounds like he has a hot potato in his mouth.
scenarios.rationale: Suspected peritonsillar abscess (Quinsy) with airway compromise risk = emergency

scenarios.input: My 6-year-old boy says his left testicle hurts a little bit. There is no swelling, no redness, and he is walking normally.
scenarios.rationale: Any acute testicular pain in a child must be treated as suspected torsion (emergency) until proven otherwise

calibration_instructions.step1: Run all scenarios through detect_concepts() and record (concept_name, similarity_score)
calibration_instructions.step2: Plot score distribution for True Positives vs True Negatives
calibration_instructions.step3: Find the threshold where all emergency scenarios (expected_level <= 2) are correctly detected
calibration_instructions.step4: Accept some False Positives — in medicine, over-caution is safer than under-caution
calibration_instructions.step5: Set SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD in emergency_detector.py to the calibrated value
calibration_instructions.note: Current default threshold = 0.52 — validate against this test set before production
